articleTitle: Sol-gel derived microstructured fiber: fabrication and characterization
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We discuss a sol-gel casting technique for fabricating microstructured optical fiber. Both the advantages and challenges associated with this fabrication method are outlined.

articleTitle: Coherent demodulation of 40-Gbit/s polarization-multiplexed QPSK signals with 16-GHz spacing after 200-km transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: 40-Gbit/s polarization-multiplexed QPSK signals with 16-GHz spacing are demodulated after 200-km transmission by using a homodyne phase-diversity receiver. The highlights of our scheme are electrical post-filtering and digital signal processing that enhance the BER performance.

articleTitle: 5120 km RZ-DPSK transmission over G652 fiber at 10 Gb/s with no optical dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report the longest unregenerated reach achieved for a 10 Gb/s return-to-zero differential phase shift keying (RZ-DPSK) system on standard dispersion fiber (G652) with no optical dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Field trial results on statistics of fast polarization changes in long haul WDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Field trials were carried out to determine the statistics of fast polarization changes in optical networks. Important data enabling the definition of speed requirements for PMD compensators and adaptive equalizers could be obtained.

articleTitle: Electrical domain compensation of optical dispersion [optical fibre communication applications]
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Recent advances in the electrical equalization of optical systems are presented in the context of standard methods. We report 10 Gb/s transmission over 60,000 ps/nm of optical dispersion from 3840 km of NDSF (non-dispersion shifted fibre).

articleTitle: ROADM subsystems and technologies
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: ROADM (reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexers) subsystems can be implemented using a variety of architectures and technologies, each with their own trade-offs in performance and functionality. This paper describes the available technology options, and corresponding subsystem features, while highlighting the key advantages and implementation challenges associated with each.

articleTitle: 10-user, truly-asynchronous OCDMA experiment with 511-chip SSFBG en/decoder and SC-based optical thresholder
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time a 10-user, truly-asynchronous, gigabit OCDMA experiment over 50 km transmission using 511-chip SSFBG encoder/decoder and supercontinuum-based optical thresholder. Suppression of both beat noise and MAI are keys to the success.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 2.5-Gslot/s optically-preamplified M-PPM with 4 photons/bit receiver sensitivity
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Photon-efficient optical communications using variable-duty-cycle M-ary pulse-position modulation (M-PPM) with coding is investigated experimentally using a simple, multi-rate nearly quantum-limited receiver with throughputs ranging from 1.25 Gbit/s, in the binary case, to 78 Mbit/s, for M=256.

articleTitle: Measurement of the dispersion tolerance of optical duobinary with an MLSE-receiver at 10.7 Gb/s
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a significant improvement in the dispersion tolerance of optical duobinary modulation when employing an MLSE instead of a standard receiver. We show that the improvement critically depends on the MLSE design.

articleTitle: Integrated DQPSK transmitters
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Integration of multiple functionality on a single chip has enabled the development of compact DQPSK transmitters for optical transmission. High performance and stable operation allow the key attributes of the DQPSK format to be demonstrated.

articleTitle: Survivable network architectures for WDM PON
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a simple self-protecting architecture for WDM PON. The protection time was less than 10 ms, and the power penalty caused by the protection process was negligible.

articleTitle: Terabit LAN with optical virtual concatenation for Grid applications with super-computers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper proposes an optical local area network that can transmit terabit-class bulk-data with low latency in a dynamic manner. A group of wavelengths is assigned to bulk-data transmission according to the latency requirement, and parallel WDM signals are transmitted with bit-phase synchronization mechanism after fast provisioning.

articleTitle: Protection of multicast sessions in WDM mesh optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We investigate the problem of protecting a multicast session in WDM mesh networks against any single link failure. Our proposed collapsed-ring dedicated 1+1 protection scheme exhibits very good performance relative to other schemes.

articleTitle: Unrepeated 210-km transmission with coherent detection and digital signal processing of 20-Gb/s QPSK signal
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate an unrepeated transmission of 20-Gb/s QPSK. signals over 210 km using coherent detection and digital signal processing. Phase estimation of the homodyne-detected QPSK signal improves the bit-error rate performance compared to differential demodulation.

articleTitle: Generation and propagation of a 1550 nm 10 Gbit/s optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexed signal over 1000m of multimode fibre using a directly modulated DFB
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: OFDM is a spectrally efficient, robust and flexible modulation format. We have theoretically and practically investigated optical OFDM at the highest ever data rate of 10 Gbit/s and successfully transmitted a signal over 1000 m of multimode fibre using a directly modulated laser transmitter.

articleTitle: A 240-GHz active mode-locked laser diode for ultra-broadband fiber-radio transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 240-GHz optical millimeter-wave signal with very narrow linewidth (<10 Hz) is generated using an active mode-locked laser diode integrated with a high-mesa electroabsorption modulator. Fiber-radio transmission of 3-Gbit/s data at 240 GHz is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Linear microwave-domain dispersion compensation of 10-Gb/s signals using heterodyne detection
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate heterodyne detection of 10-Gb/s signals, and subsequent linear compensation of fiber chromatic dispersion in the microwave domain. We achieve 375-km transmission (with 2-dB penalty) over standard single-mode fiber using duobinary modulation and a single passive microwave dispersion-compensating element.

articleTitle: 320 Gbit/s clock recovery with electro-optical PLL using a bidirectionally operated electroabsorption modulator as phase comparator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 40 GHz clock signal is recovered from a single-polarisation 320 Gbit/s data signal using a bidirectionally operated electroabsorption modulator (EAM) as phase comparator. The clock recovery was operated in a single-polarisation 320 Gbit/s, 160 km transmission experiment.

articleTitle: Experimental results on the simultaneous transmission of two 2.5 Gbps optical-CDMA channels and a 10 Gbps OOK channel within the same WDM window
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and experimentally validate a novel method for transmitting several OCDMA channels in the unused bandwidth of a single WDM channel thus allowing the OCDMA and SONET signals to share the same WDM channel.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a complete 12-port Terabit capacity optical packet switching fabric
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report on the implementation of a complete 12-port Data Vortex optical packet switching fabric containing 36 fully-interconnected nodes. Correct routing behavior is verified for 14-channel WDM packets, and latencies below 60 ns are achieved.

articleTitle: Electronic dispersion compensation by signal predistortion using a dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose the technique of signal predistortion using a dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator and nonlinear digital filters, and demonstrate compensation of 13600 ps/nm, equivalent to 800 km of standard single mode fibre, at 10 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation for wireless LAN, Ethernet and UWB coexistence on hybrid radio-over-fiber picocells
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The performance of IEEE 802.11a and gigabit Ethernet coexisting with ultra-wideband is evaluated in a low-cost VCSEL-based ROF channel for wired and wireless picocell applications. Experimental results showing such services in an ROF environment of various lengths are presented.

articleTitle: DWDM reach extension of a GPON to 135 km
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report operation of a GPON (gigabit-capable passive optical network) (2.488 Gbit/s downstream, 1.244 Gbit/s upstream) over 135 km giving performance consistent with ITU-T standards. Advanced DWDM equipment is used to extend the physical reach and provide fibre gain.

articleTitle: Field trial of a 40 Gbit/s PSBT channel upgrade to an installed 1700 km 10 Gbit/s system
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents the results of three practical experiments proving the viability of 40 Gbit/s phase-shaped binary transmission (PSBT) channel upgrade to existing 10G systems supporting 50 GHz channel spacing: (a) lab experiments with a fully loaded 1000 km 80-channel 10 Gbit/s system upgraded with two 40 Gbit/s PSBT channels, (b) an 850 km field trial of 40 Gbit/s PSBT channel upgrade to an installed 10 Gbit/s system and installed fiber, (c) an extension of the 850 km field trial to 1700 km via optical loop back. The 10 Gbit/s system was left as originally provisioned and all link control loops were active during the trials. Error free performance after FEC was achieved for all three experimental configurations, proving flexible and seamless 40 Gbit/s PSBT channel upgrade to existing 10 Gbit/s systems is possible and practical.

articleTitle: DWDM long haul network deployment for the Verizon GNI nationwide network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a 226 node, 128 channel Raman gain based DWDM system being deployed by Verizon GNI to create a nationwide automated optical network carrying 10 Gb/s traffic and offering 40 Gb/s traffic capability.

articleTitle: 200 Gchip/s, 16-label simultaneous multiple-optical encoder/decoder and its application to optical packet switching
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 200 Gchip/s, 16-label simultaneous multiple-optical encoder/decoder has been fabricated; it generates and recognizes simultaneously multiple codes in a parallel manner. 10 Gbit/s optical packet switching with the test encoder/decoder was demonstrated experimentally. Optical packets with different labels were switched according to their own destination label based on multiple label processing.

articleTitle: Flexible transport at 10-Gb/s from 0 to 675 km (11,500 ps/nm) using a chirp-managed laser, no DCF, and a dynamically adjustable dispersion-compensating receiver
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate continuous detectability of 10-Gb/s data from 0 to 675 km of standard single mode fiber without inline dispersion compensation using a combination of a chirp-managed laser and tunable optical and electronic dispersion compensation at the receiver.

articleTitle: 321 W average power, 1 GHz, 20 ps, 1060 nm pulsed fiber MOPA source
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Pulses from a gain-switched laser diode were amplified in a fiber MOPA system to produce in excess of 320 W of average power in 20 ps pulses at 1 GHz repetition rate at 1060 nm.

articleTitle: Penalty-free dispersion-managed soliton transmission over 100 km low loss PCF
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We successfully fabricated a 100 km-long, low loss (0.3 dB/km) photonic crystal fiber (PCF) with the lowest Rayleigh scattering coefficient. We achieved the first penalty-free dispersion-managed soliton transmission over 100 km PCF at 10 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Low timing jitter, 5 GHz optical pulses from monolithic two-section passively mode-locked 1250/1310 nm quantum dot lasers for high-speed optical interconnects
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Sub-picosecond timing jitter is demonstrated for 5 GHz, <10 ps optical pulses generated from monolithic passively mode-locked quantum dot lasers. Their low cost, compact size and DC-biased operation make them ideal for high speed optical interconnects.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of optical burst and circuit switched networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents quantitative performance comparisons between the OBS and OCS networks. The simulation results indicate that, under identical traffic demand and network capacity, OBS networks achieve a higher throughput than OCS networks.

articleTitle: Optical burst amplification using EDFA with fast feedback control
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show that optical bursts can be amplified with suppressed gain transients using an erbium-doped fiber amplifier controlled by a fast electrical feedback loop. Transmission without power penalty is demonstrated for various burst lengths.

articleTitle: New architecture for an all optical network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper describes the service scenarios and economic analysis that lead to the conclusion that a radial approach for optical access and core is required. It then discusses a way forward for the evolution of the access and core optical network architecture that could provide a high capacity, multi-service capability to all types of customers with minimum number of tiers and network nodes at costs significantly lower than traditional price declines could realise.

articleTitle: Correlation sensitive Viterbi equalization of 10 Gb/s signals in bandwidth limited receivers [optical receivers]
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Viterbi equalization in bandwidth limited receivers requires correlation sensitive algorithms more than increased state algorithms. The application of both enables equalization at 10 Gb/s with 1 dB add on penalty, if a 2.5 Gb/s receiver is applied.

articleTitle: Application of fundamental-mode cutoff for novel amplifiers and lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Depressed-cladding fibers with fundamental-mode cutoffs provide high distributed losses at long wavelengths and low losses at short wavelengths. ASE suppression at 4-level transitions enables gain on shorter-wavelength, 3-level transitions. We discuss applications to Er-, Tm-, Nd-, and Yb-doped fiber amplifiers.

articleTitle: Optical burst switching network testbed in Japan
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A five-year (2001-2005) government-supported R&D initiative, "optical burst switching network", is introduced. It is a comprehensive program, including network architecture, wavelength reservation protocol, ultrafast processing of control packets, and switching fabric.

articleTitle: Impedance-detuned high-contrast vertical cavity semiconductor switch
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report an all-optical semiconductor gate optimized for high-contrast switching. Using a pump signal with an intensity of less than /spl sim/25 KW/cm/sup 2/, we demonstrate a 30-dB contrast ratio for 10-GHz pulses with energy of 0.05 pJ.

articleTitle: SOA-based regenerative amplification of phase noise degraded DPSK signals
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: SOA-based regenerative amplification of phase noise degraded DPSK signals is demonstrated for a single and two non-demultiplexed channels. Q-factor improvement is 1.6 dB in the single channel and about 0.8 dB in the two channel regime.

articleTitle: 40-Gb/s colorless tunable dispersion compensator with 1000-ps/nm tuning range employing a planar lightwave circuit and a deformable mirror
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a tunable dispersion compensator for 40-Gb/s signals consisting of a waveguide grating router and a deformable mirror. It has an adjustment range of /spl plusmn/500 ps/nm and a 100-GHz free-spectral range.

articleTitle: Towards integrated polarization diversity: design, fabrication, and characterization of integrated polarization splitters and rotators
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Integrated mode-evolution-based polarization splitters and rotators were designed with rigorous electromagnetic simulations and fabricated with a unique multilayer fabrication strategy. Prototype devices demonstrated effective splitting and rotating of polarization with low cross-talk.

articleTitle: High performance planar lightwave circuit triplexer with passive optical assembly
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: High performance, compact planar lightwave circuit based triplexers have been built and tested. The triplexers utilize lasers, photodiodes and filters that have been adapted to enable passive optical assembly of the triplexer.

articleTitle: Self-configuring intelligent control for short reach 100Gb/s optical packet routing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An advanced control architecture is proposed which recognizes and configures new connections, automatically performs calibration and initiates the routing of 100 Gb/s data packets. The scheme is proposed for high capacity, low overhead, short reach networking.

articleTitle: Tuneable All-Fiber/sup /spl reg// delay-line interferometer for DPSK demodulation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An All-Fiber/sup /spl reg// tunable Mach-Zehnder delay line interferometer was developed for differential phase shift keying (DPSK) demodulation. Low loss and high isolation are maintained in a compact package by annealing the fibers at high temperature to relieve bending stresses. Reliability data is presented.

articleTitle: 3R regeneration of a 40-Gbit/s optical signal by optical parametric amplification in a highly-nonlinear fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate wavelength-shift-free 3R-regeneration of 40-Gbit/s optical RZ signal by OPA with a clock-modulated pump in highly-nonlinear fiber. The power penalty is improved by 2.6 dB, and the signal power is amplified by 7 dB.

articleTitle: Novel modulation scheme for optical continuous-phase frequency-shift keying
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a novel scheme for continuous-phase frequency-shift-keying (CP-FSK) optical modulation. By synchronizing the baseband signal with the clock for sideband generation, external CP-FSK modulation is demonstrated at 10 Gbit/s for the first time.

articleTitle: Dynamic provisioning with reliability guarantee and resource optimization for differentiated services in WDM mesh networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a reliability analysis for shared-path-protected WDM mesh networks. We develop a cost-effective provisioning approach to provide differentiated services to carry connections with both reliability guarantee and resource optimization.

articleTitle: The OptIPuter, Quartzite, and Starlight projects: a campus to global-scale testbed for optical technologies enabling LambdaGrid computing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Dedicated optical connections have significant advantages over shared Internet connections. The OptIPuter project (www.optiputer.net) uses medical and earth sciences imaging as application drivers. Quartzite (UCSD) and Starlight (Chicago) create unique combinations of OEO routers and OOO and wavelength-selective optical switches.

articleTitle: Delay distributed VCAT for efficient data-optical transport
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We introduce a novel scheme that flexibly distributes the differential delays in virtual concatenation (VCAT) paths in SONET/SDH networks. We show that this increases the utilization of the network in carrying dynamic traffic and reduces the total buffer requirements.

articleTitle: Bidirectional single fiber transmission based on a RSOA ONU for FTTH using FSK-IM modulation formats
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Full-duplex bidirectional transmission using FSK modulation for downstream and remote IM using a reflective SOA for upstream in a single-fiber WDM-PON access network is demonstrated. The system shows proper operation at 1 Gbit/s to 30 km reach.

articleTitle: Electronic dispersion compensation for 10 Gigabit communication links over FDDI legacy multimode fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate measured results from two different EDC architectures, a feed forward equalizer (FFE) and a decision feedback equalizer (DFE). These are used to compensate for ISI caused by modal dispersion in highly band-limited multi-mode fiber links.

articleTitle: SiGe equalizer IC for PMD mitigation and signal optimization of 40 Gbits/s transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A SiGe equalizer IC has been developed to mitigate fiber-induced and electro-optical distortions for 40 Gbits/s optical transmission. Experiments show 50% improvement in 1st-order PMD tolerance for 1 dBQ penalty and 1 dB improvement in back-to-back OSNR sensitivity.

articleTitle: Simultaneous reception of both quadratures of 40-Gb/s DQPSK using a simple monolithic demodulator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a novel device that demodulates both quadratures of the optical differential quadrature phase shift keying (DQPSK) format in a single interferometer. We present simultaneous measurements of both DQPSK quadratures at 42.7-Gb/s.

articleTitle: Multi-step-index bismuth-based highly nonlinear fiber with low propagation loss and splicing loss
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Propagation loss and practical fusion-splicing loss of bismuth-based fibers are reduced to 0.8 dB/m and 2.6 dB/point, respectively, while maintaining high nonlinearity of 1100 W/sup -1/ km/sup -1/ by modifying the glass composition and eliminating the cladding mode.

articleTitle: Fundamental limitations of slow-light optical buffers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show that slow-light optical delay-line buffers are constrained by fundamental physical limitations. We compare the capabilities of a variety of buffer technologies including electromagnetically induced transparency, population pulsations, photonic crystal filters, and fibre-based delay lines.

articleTitle: PMD-insensitive DOP-based OSNR monitoring by spectral SOP measurements
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a DOP (degree of polarization) based OSNR (optical signal-to-noise ratio) monitoring method with spectral SOP (state of polarization) measurement to perform OSNR measurements insensitive to PMD (polarization-mode dispersion). Measurements at OSNR = 25 dB and DGD (differential group delay) = 32% of bitslot are performed with a standard deviation of 0.67 dB.

articleTitle: 1-km transmission of 10 Gbit/s optical signal over legacy MMF using mode limiting transmission and incoherent light source
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: 10 Gbit/s optical signals were transmitted through legacy multimode fibers (MMF) by using mode limiting and incoherent light sources. Stable transmission through a 1-km-long MMF was realized by inserting a singlemode fiber (SMF) at midpoint.

articleTitle: C/S-band WDM-PON employing colorless bidirectional transceivers and SOA-based broadband light sources
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a low-cost C/S-band WDM-PON employing colorless uncooled bidirectional transceivers and SOA-based broadband light sources. Colorless operations over 32 DWDM channels are demonstrated from -20 to 80/spl deg/C in 155-Mb/s bidirectional transmissions over 25 km.

articleTitle: A testbed for optical burst switching network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a testbed for optical burst switching network based on the priority JET scheme, and demonstrates flexible node architectures. Also experimental results verify functions of various modules, flexibility and stable operation of the testbed.

articleTitle: Performance of MQW InP Mach-Zehnder modulators for advanced modulation formats
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The performance of InP modulators is investigated for duobinary and differential phase-shift key transmission. We demonstrate that despite nonlinear phase-voltage characteristics and residual absorption, InP devices give excellent performance comparable to ideal Mach-Zehnder modulators.

articleTitle: A stable widely tunable laser using a silica-waveguide triple-ring resonator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A tunable laser consisting of a silica-waveguide triple-ring resonator connected directly to a semiconductor optical amplifier is presented. Stable single-mode, grid-hopping free and full-band wavelength-digitally-tuning operations with 50-GHz channel spacing are successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Re-optimization strategies to maximize traffic-carrying readiness in WDM survivable mesh networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and compare four re-optimization strategies for mesh survivable networks. We show how these strategies improve the network's ability to carry future random-arrival traffic.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of modulation formats for 40 Gbit/s DWDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The performance of various modulation formats, namely OOK, DPSK and DQPSK with and without RZ carving, were experimentally compared to clarify the optimum modulation formats for 40 Gbit/s DWDM transmission systems with 50 GHz channel spacing.

articleTitle: Fully-programmable ring resonator based integrated photonic circuit for phase coherent applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a novel reconfigurable ring resonator based integrated photonic chip with ultra-fine frequency resolution for spectral phase encoding. A spectrally efficient four-user OCDMA system is shown to operate at 2.5 Gb/s with BER< 10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: An empirical model for high yield manufacturing of 10Gb/s negative chirp InP Mach-Zehnder modulators
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A statistically valid empirical model is used to optimize InP Mach-Zehnder modulators to achieve high yield, wide tunability, record low insertion loss, and dispersion-limited reach superior to that of -0.7/spl alpha/ LiNbO/sub 3/ modulators.

articleTitle: Dynamic control of wavelength switching and shuttering operations in a broadband tunable DS-DBR laser module
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Dynamic control of channel switching is demonstrated in a DS-DBR laser module using an integrated optical amplifier as a shutter. Switching time between locked channels is less than 6 ms and frequency deviation less than 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated 40 Gb/s wavelength converter with multi-frequency laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An all-optical wavelength-switch module at 40 Gb/s is monolithically integrated in InP by combining an SOA-based wavelength converter and a fast-tunable 8-channel multi-frequency laser. Error-free operation is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Prototype demonstration of IP multicasting over optical networks with dynamic point-to-multipoint configuration
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a novel overlay multicasting architecture: IP multicasting over optical networks with dynamic point-to-multipoint configuration. Experimental results show that the proposed architecture exhibits better performance than pure IP multicasting under heavy traffic load.

articleTitle: Fiber lasers for lidar
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Advances in fiber laser technology can be used to further the capabilities of lidar remote sensing systems. The paper provides an overview of lidar requirements, where current fiber technology can play a role, and advances needed for future systems.

articleTitle: Experimental study of the impact of optical confinement on saturation effects in SOA
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Measurements of SOA with various optical confinements show that low confinement devices are not saturated by ASE. This allows them to have good inversion factors at their input section, which leads to state-of-the-art noise factors.

articleTitle: Shared protection for multicast sessions in mesh networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We investigate optimal sharing among backups of several multicast sessions in an optical mesh network. Our cross-sharing approach provides significant cost-savings of backup resources relative to arc-disjoint and self-sharing approaches, especially for a large number of sessions.

articleTitle: 160 Gb/s SOA-based wavelength converter assisted by an optical bandpass filter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate an error-free 160 Gb/s SOA-based optical wavelength converter. Assisted by an optical bandpass filter, an effective recovery time of 3 ps is achieved in an SOA, which ensures 160 Gb/s operation.

articleTitle: 80 Gb/s ETDM transmitter with a traveling-wave electroabsorption modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have demonstrated non-return-to-zero data transmission at 80 Gb/s using an ETDM (electronic time division multiplexing) fiberoptic transmitter consisting of a segmented traveling-wave electroabsorption modulator with integrated termination resistor and a SiGe electronic multiplexer.

articleTitle: 40G over 10G infrastructure - dispersion management issues
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Transmission at 40G over a 10G infrastructure needs compatible dispersion management. The optimum chromatic dispersion at 40 Gbit/s is investigated, and its adjustment to a 10 Gbit/s infrastructure over SMF or NZDSF fiber types is discussed.

articleTitle: 200 km CWDM transmission using a hybrid amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report a 60 nm bandwidth SOA (semiconductor optical amplifier)-Raman hybrid amplifier for CWDM systems in which the Raman section increases overall system gain and reduces SOA gain tilt. The amplifier module is used in a 4-channel, 200-km CWDM transmission experiment.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of the signal degradation in WDM transmission through coherent crosstalk caused by a fast tunable SG-DBR laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Novel results are presented on thermally induced wavelength drift in a fast tunable SG-DBR laser and the signal impairments caused in a 10 Gb/s transmission system through coherent crosstalk generated during each wavelength switching process.

articleTitle: Modeling RZ-DPSK transmission - simulations and measurements for an installed submarine system
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We model RZ-DPSK transmission in an installed 6,550 km transatlantic submarine system. Simulations agree well with measurements. Simulations predict that nonlinear noise does not eliminate the RZ-DPSK advantage over RZ-OOK, even for trans-Pacific distances.

articleTitle: Load-balanced architecture for dynamic traffic
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a novel and practical scheme for carrying dynamic data traffic over circuits at lower costs than existing architectures. We demonstrate its effectiveness in handling burstiness as well as long-term variations in traffic patterns.

articleTitle: Experimental comparison of the RZ-DPSK and NRZ-DPSK modulation formats
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The RZ-DPSK and NRZ-DPSK modulation formats were experimentally compared using installed undersea fiber links. Our results show a 1-1.5 dB RZ benefit with optimized RZ modulation depth for both 25-GHz and 33-GHz spaced channels.

articleTitle: New optical switching fabric architecture incorporating load balanced parallel rapidly switching all-optical variable delay buffer arrays
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a novel optical switching fabric architecture employing load-balanced parallel all-optical variable delay buffer arrays and demonstrate more than an order of magnitude performance enhancement in terms of packet loss rate, delay and jitter.

articleTitle: Reduction of phase noise by mid-link spectral inversion in a DPSK based transmission system
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show, in an 800 km SSMF (standard single mode fiber) transmission experiment, that mid-link spectral inversion can be employed to reduce the effect of phase noise (Gordon-Mollenauer noise) on DPSK (differential phase-shift-keying) by over two decades in BER.

articleTitle: Nationwide GMPLS field trial using different types (MPLS/TDM/lambda) of switching capable equipment from multiple vendors
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A GMPLS field trial using different types of switching capable equipments from multiple vendors was conducted on a nationwide scale and the setup of MPLS/TDM/lambda hierarchical LSP was successfully achieved ensuring GMPLS interoperability in a multilayer for the first time.

articleTitle: Ultra small and low power consumption 8ch variable optical attenuator multiplexer (V-AWG) using multi-chip PLC integration technology
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have developed an ultra small 8ch variable optical attenuator multiplexer (V-AWG) with excellent optical performance using multi-chip planar lightwave circuit (PLC) technology. The insertion loss is 5.0 dB for a flat-top spectrum and the polarization dependent loss (PDL) at 15 dB attenuation is 0.4 dB. The module is 70 /spl times/ 45 /spl times/ 14 mm including the control board and this is 1/20 the size of a multi source agreement (MSA) type V-AWG Moreover, the total power consumption of this 8ch module is only 0.8 W.

articleTitle: Highly reliable AlGaInAs buried heterostructure lasers for uncooled 10 Gb/s direct modulation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: High reliability (estimated median lifetime of 240,000 hours) of 1.3 /spl mu/m AlGaInAs buried heterostructure lasers has been demonstrated by more than 10,000 hours accelerated aging tests. Distributed-feedback lasers have successfully operated at 10 Gb/s at 95/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Use of downstream inverse-RZ signal for upstream data re-modulation in a WDM passive optical network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and experimentally investigate a novel WDM-PON architecture using inverse-RZ modulated centralized light sources. The finite optical power in each bit of the downstream IRZ signal can greatly facilitate the upstream data re-modulation.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 1.3 /spl mu/m quantum key distribution (QKD) compatibility with 1.5 /spl mu/m metropolitan wavelength division multiplexed (WDM) systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Impairment-free multiplexing and transmission of a 1.3 /spl mu/m QKD system with a multi-wavelength 1.5 /spl mu/m metropolitan area DWDM system is demonstrated with a quantum BER of 4.6 % over 25 km of standard singlemode fiber.

articleTitle: Operational cost reduction using ASON/ASTN
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: ASON/ASTN technologies promise automated network operations, significantly reducing costs. This paper presents some results from a process-based quantitative approach analyzing the reductions in operational costs to be expected for networks operators using these technologies.

articleTitle: The Mars laser communications demonstration project: truly ultralong-haul optical transport
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present an overview of the Mars laser communications demonstration (MLCD), a joint project between NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology (JPL), and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Lincoln Laboratory (MIT/LL). MLCD's goal is to demonstrate the first high-rate, freespace laser communications link from deep space back to Earth. The lasercom flight terminal will be flown on the Mars Telecommunications Orbiter, to be launched by NASA in 2009, and will demonstrate a technology which has the potential of vastly improving NASA's ability to communicate throughout the solar system.

articleTitle: High-performance distributed Raman amplification systems: practical aspects and field trial results
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We introduce high-performance distributed Raman amplification (DRA) systems employing a DRA/EDFA hybrid amplifier scheme with practical aspects based on safety considerations. We also describe successful field trial results using the scheme with high pump-efficiency.

articleTitle: A 400Gbps backplane switch with 10Gbps/port optical I/O interfaces based on OIP (optical interconnection as IP of a CMOS library)
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 400 Gbit/s backplane switch was developed with a low-cost, small-size, 8-channel 10 Gbit/s/port optical I/O and a SiGe Bi-CMOS switch LSI on a 60/spl times/60-mm-square BGA package. It indicates the applicability of OIP for high throughput backplane interconnections.

articleTitle: Generation of ultra-flat SPM-broadened spectra in a highly nonlinear fiber using pulse pre-shaping in a fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a new approach to generating spectrally flat supercontinuum pulses based on seeding a commercial nonlinear fibre with pump pulses shaped using a superstructured fiber Bragg grating. Experimental results confirm the viability of the approach.

articleTitle: Monolithically-integrated 40 Gbit/s widely-tunable transmitter using series push-pull Mach-Zehnder modulator SOA and sampled-grating DBR laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A monolithically integrated widely-tunable transmitter using a series push-pull Mach-Zehnder electrode structure with a semiconductor optical amplifier and SGDBR laser is presented suitable for 40 Gbit/s systems with tuning over 34 nm.

articleTitle: All-fibre frequency conversion in long periodically poled silica fibres
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Efficient all-fibre frequency doubling of 1.5 /spl mu/m pulsed fibre laser has been demonstrated. 3.6 mW of second-harmonic light in fundamental mode was produced by quasiphase-matching in a 11.5 cm long periodically poled germanosilicate fibre. The /spl chi//sup (2)/-grating was fabricated by continuous periodic-UV-erasure.

articleTitle: Dynamic routing with preplanned congestion avoidance for survivable optical burst-switched (OBS) networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We develop dynamic routing mechanisms for preplanned congestion avoidance in OBS networks. Based on our routing mechanisms, we propose a new protection approach against failures which significantly improves network throughput and survivability.

articleTitle: Whole C-band, repetition rate tunable optical pulse generation using a high-resolution arrayed-waveguide grating and an optical comb generator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Short optical pulses with a center wavelength of 1527-1563 nm and with a repetition rate of 9.75-10.25 GHz are successfully generated with a 10-GHz resolution arrayed-waveguide grating with integrated phase and amplitude modulators.

articleTitle: Tunable single-frequency ytterbium-sensitized erbium-doped fiber MOPA source with 150 W (51.8 dBm) of output power at 1563 nm
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A single-frequency, single-mode ytterbium-sensitized erbium-doped fiber master-oscillator power-amplifier generated 150 W of continuous-wave output power at 1563 nm with 33% slope efficiency and was tuned in the range of 1546 to 1566 nm at >125 W.

articleTitle: Stimulated-Brillouin-scattering suppression using a single modulator in two-pump parametric architectures
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We achieve synchronous phase modulation in a two-pump parametric processor using one phase modulator to provide stimulated Brillouin scattering suppression to both pumps. Simple frequency tuning controls the pump synchronization.

articleTitle: A wide-area carrier-distributed WDM-based access network accommodating GbE and 10 GbE services
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper describes a wide-area carrier-distributed WDM-based access network accommodating GbE and 10 GbE services over metro/access areas extending several tens of kilometers. A transmission experiment is conducted by using the colorless ONUs of GbE and 10 GbE and its performance is evaluated.

articleTitle: Recent progress in Bi-EDF technologies
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Bismuth based erbium doped fiber exhibits inherent features which cannot be realized with silica based EDF. Extended L-band amplification, high gain C+L band amplification for coarse WDM and short pulse amplification are reported.

articleTitle: Demonstration of an in-band auxiliary channel for path trace in photonic networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a new method for encoding path trace labels, or other management information, into WDM lightpaths in a network. Management data is extracted successfully using low-speed receivers without wavelength filters over the necessary wide range of optical signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a novel all-fiber bandpass acousto-optic tunable filter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An all-fiber tunable bandpass filter is demonstrated. A dual acousto-optic grating inside a Sagnac loop changes the polarization of the light over a narrow bandwidth which redirects the light from reflection to the transmission port.

articleTitle: Pump-to-signal FWM of co-pumped Raman amplifier for remote pumps supervisory
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A novel remote pump monitoring scheme based on pump-to-signal four-wave mixing in a 50 m highly nonlinear dispersion shifted photonic crystal fiber is proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: OFO - Electrical processing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The technical challenges and potential applications of Block Turbo Code based soft-decision FEC are discussed. Its large coding gain and the consequent reduction of fiber nonlinearity effects will have a positive impact on the cost -effectiveness of optical networks.

articleTitle: A technique for the measurement of the residual birefringence in erbium-doped fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The erbium doped fiber is modeled as the combination of a linear and circular distributed retarder. Data analysis is performed using Stokes vectors, Mueller calculus and the Poincare description of polarization.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of polarization mode dispersion emulators for low background autocorrelation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show that the frequency correlation of multi-section PMD emulators can be minimized for any given set of birefringent elements. We present a model describing the underlying cause of the correlation, which is verified using simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-function integrated AWG devices
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report a new approach for dynamic controlling of AWG temperature utilizing on-chip thin film thermo-optic heaters. This enables integration of multiple optical functions with AWG on a single chip platform, to make high performance and low cost ROADM components.

articleTitle: OFJ - Pulsed lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Precision stabilization of mode-locked lasers, by locking them to optical frequency transitions, has lead to remarkable advances in high accuracy frequency standards and is enabling improvements of time and frequency transfer over fiber.

articleTitle: Self-starting, high-repetition rate picosecond pulse generation using stimulated Brillouin scattering in optical fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a self-starting optical-pulse source at 10 GHz using an optoelectronic-oscillator based on an EML. The RF-component is generated from stimulated-Brillouin-scattering in optical fiber. Different types of optical fibers are used respectively to generate optical pulses at different repetition rates.

articleTitle: 100-nm cascaded hybrid doped fiber amplifier for coarse wavelength division multiplexing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A hybrid amplifier spanning from 1468-1568 nm is constructed by cascading a thulium-doped fiber amplifier pumped at 690 nm and 1400 nm and a cerium co-doped high concentration wideband erbium-doped fiber amplifier.

articleTitle: Widely tunable sub-picosecond compression of 40 GHz externally-modulated pulse train using 1.4 km long comb-like profiled fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrated the compression to 500 fs of a 40 GHz externally modulated pulse train with a wideband tunablity over 1530-1560 nm. A comb-like profiled fiber plays an important role in the widely tunable operation.

articleTitle: Highly birefringent hollow-core photonic bandgap fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A highly birefringent hollow-core photonic bandgap fiber is fabricated and characterized. The fiber group birefringence is found to be 0.025 at 1550 nm through wavelength scanning method and direct measurement of differential group delay.

articleTitle: A pixelized VOA based on liquid crystal on silicon
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have fabricated a 512-pixel liquid crystal VOA (variable optical attenuator) with biased PWM based on liquid crystal on silicon, using ITiO as a common electrode. The VOA is suitable for making tunable filters with low driver voltage.

articleTitle: Ultra-long transmission performance evaluation of 43Gbit/s CSRZ-DPSK DWDM signal using 4,300km DMF line
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: More than 10,000 km transmission capability was confirmed with 43 Gbit/s CSRZ-DPSK and conventional DMF lines. But the polarization dependent effects never guaranteed the complete stability at 4,300 km where a Q-factor margin of 5 dB was obtained in the short-term evaluation.

articleTitle: Pump-to-Stokes relative intensity noise (RIN) transfer in Raman fiber lasers: observations and modeling
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: By analogy with Raman amplifiers we explored pump-to-Stokes RIN transfer for Raman lasers. We report direct measurement of the effect and its analytical model. RIN associated with pump longitudinal mode beating deteriorates Raman laser performances.

articleTitle: A fast and accurate numerical tool to model the mode properties of photonic-bandgap fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a new mode solver that models photonic-bandgap fibers /spl sim/ 1,000 times faster that existing codes. Finding the indices and fields of the modes of a fiber now takes only /spl sim/ 6 seconds per mode per wavelength on a personal computer.

articleTitle: Optical self-similar cluster switching (OSCS)
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The objective of OSCS is to solve the obstacles brought by the traffic self-similarity. Our analyses and simulation results show that the burst flooding effect caused by the traffic self-similarity can be successfully smoothed out by using OSCS.

articleTitle: Quantum noise properties of parametric devices driven by two pump waves
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: In parametric amplifiers and frequency-convertors driven by two pump waves, each signal sideband is coupled to three idler sidebands. Formulas are derived for the signal and idler noise-figures of these devices.

articleTitle: Increasing FTTH reliability between premise and indoor lines
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An analysis of faults subsequent to service starting on premises and indoor FTTH lines, with countermeasures which were implemented. As a result, the reliability of FTTH is getting nearly the same as for metal lines.

articleTitle: All-optical add-drop node for packet-switched networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrated all-optical packet add/drop for all-optical packet-switched networks. Intelligent all-optical add-drop of packets is performed based on all-optical processing of packet headers. The header and payload rates are 5 Gb/s and 10 Gb/s respectively.

articleTitle: Photonic bus with multi-channel selection on a SOI chip
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have demonstrated a silicon-on-insulator based photonic bus with integrated splitters and multi-channel optical wavelength selection. The integrated photonic bus has demonstrated a 33+ dB optical crosstalk and a 32+ dB extinction ratio with two-stage of Mach-Zehnder attenuators.

articleTitle: A simple and low-cost 1625 nm OTDR monitoring system for 350 km WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An SOA-based 1625 nm OTDR (optical time domain reflectometry) monitoring system in a bypass configuration is successfully demonstrated for a 350 km WDM network. No power penalty is observed in the 10 Gb/s WDM transmissions when the OTDR signal is on.

articleTitle: Modeling and experimental verification of infusion speed of liquids in photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A theoretical method for predicting infusion time of liquids in microcapillaries is formulated. Through a microscopical, a fluorescent, and, finally, through a reflectometric measurement method, the model is successfully verified in real photonic crystal fibers.

articleTitle: Experimental comparisons of DPSK and OOK in long haul transmission with 10Gbit/s signals, DMF span and Raman assisted EDFA
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We compare tolerance to self phase modulation (SPM) and cross phase modulation (XPM) of CS-RZ DPSK signals and CS-RZ OOK signals experimentally. The advantage of DPSK could be maintained after 7200 km transmission using dispersion management fiber (DMF) spans of 150 km and Raman assisted EDFA.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental study of the fundamental mode propagation phase temperature sensitivity in air-core photonic-bandgap fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We measured the dependence on temperature of the phase of the fundamental mode of air-core photonic-bandgap fibers. The expected weaker dependence (factor of 3.6-5.2) compared to conventional fibers is quantitatively well explained by a simple model.

articleTitle: Design and demonstration of Gigabit spectrum-sliced WDM systems employing directly modulated super luminescent diodes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: For realizing spectrum-sliced WDM systems with over 1 Gbps per channel, this paper elucidates the slicing bandwidth that maximizes the loss budget between transmitters and receivers as well as demonstrates a directly modulated super luminescent diode.

articleTitle: Modified Jones matrix for optical PMD compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We numerically simulate the average frequency dependence of the coupling that occurs between signal components in the two principal states of polarization and employ our results to define an improved transfer matrix for PMD compensation.

articleTitle: High power handling capability of liquid crystal variable optical attenuator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Liquid-crystal variable optical attenuator (LC-VOA) has been assembled and tested for high power application. The results demonstrated the high power tolerance of LC-VOA and its superior characteristics for EDFA applications.

articleTitle: 1-cm/sup 2/-size Er-doped waveguide based on bismuthate glass for compact amplifier with >15 dB gain at whole C-band
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 1-cm/sup 2/ size spiral Er-doped waveguide chip having gain values of >15 dB and output powers higher than 12 dBm at the whole C-band is realized by using a multicomponent bismuthate glass waveguide.

articleTitle: Planar short-multimode waveguide evanescently-coupled balanced photodetectors with fully depleted and partially depleted absorber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report short-multimode waveguide evanescently-coupled balanced photodetectors with fully-depleted (PIN) and partially-depleted (PDA) absorber. These devices have the advantages of broad bandwidth, high saturation current, simple fabrication technology and potential high responsivity.

articleTitle: Optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.

articleTitle: Optical devices for biomedical applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The recent availability of high-performance light sources and miniature optical components in the telecommunications sector has enabled the development of powerful new diagnostic technologies for biology and medicine. Recent advances in this field is presented.

articleTitle: Field trial of 40-Gbit/s wavelength path quality assurance using GMPLS-controlled all-optical 2R regenerator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have successfully demonstrated a field trial of 40-Gbit/s wavelength path quality assurance by applying a GMPLS-controlled all-optical 2R regenerator that is incorporated in a multilayer integration system among GMPLS control, measurement, and data planes.

articleTitle: Field trial of granularity-flexible reconfigurable OADM with wavelength-packet-selective switch using concurrent generation technique of optical code label and payload data
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate the first field trial of a granularity-flexible ROADM (reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexing) network with a wavelength-packet-selective switch using concurrent generation technique of address-reconfigurable optical code label and payload. Error-free operations for all 16-wavelength channels are obtained over 90-km transmission.

articleTitle: On wavelength management for restoration in WDM ring networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper discusses two schemes of managing wavelengths for restoration in WDM ring networks. Our results show that a clever management scheme with limited transparent ring interconnection would improve the wavelength utilization up to 71%.

articleTitle: Individual control of multiple AWGs on a monolithic chip using integrated thin film heaters and sensors
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Localized and independent temperature control of multiple arrayed waveguide gratings (AWGs) on a monolithic chip using integrated thin film heaters and sensors is demonstrated and applied to integrated PLC devices.

articleTitle: Raman enhanced S-band fiber optic parametric amplifier and S/C band wavelength converter: experiment and simulations
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate 10 dB gain enhancement in S-band optical parametric amplification, 10 dB net conversion efficiency enhancement, and S/C band wavelength conversion by simultaneous Raman amplification using a highly nonlinear fiber. Numerical simulations support the experimental results.

articleTitle: OFF - 40 Gb/s and beyond
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrated transmission of 16O-Gb/s OTDM signals comprising eight 20-Crb/s 2- bitlsymbol ASK-DPSK tributary channels over 200 km of installed fiber to investigate the effect of bandwidth compression on transmission impairment due to polarization mode dispersion.

articleTitle: Effects of chirp mechanism on spectrum broadening of external modulators
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show that a LiNbO/sub 3/ Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) with optical unbalancing in the two waveguides produces a chirped NRZ data stream without inducing spectral broadening as it happens with conventional chirped MZM (which employ electrical asymmetry).

articleTitle: Multi-channel PMD compensation based on distributed polarization control [fiber optic transmission applications]
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We proposed a multi-channel PMD (polarization mode dispersion) compensation technique based on distributed polarization control. The results show that the proposed technique has better performance than the multi-channel PMD compensation technique using a single PMD compensator.

articleTitle: Field transmission of 8/spl times/170 Gbit/s over high loss SSMF link using third order distributed Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report transmission of 1/spl times/170 Gbit/s over 61 dB and 8/spl times/170 Gbit/s over 44 dB attenuating links in the network of a major European network operator. Third order distributed Raman amplification established long span configurations bridging, respectively, 210 km and 165 km repeaterless span.

articleTitle: 100-nm tuning range, picosecond pulse generation employing a PM fiber loop filter in a mode-locked SOA ring laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Picosecond-pulses with a center-wavelength spanning from 1489 nm to 1589 nm is generated by a harmonically mode-locked fiber laser that exploits a SOA to provide both optical gain and mode-locking. Optical pulses with a tuning range of 100 nm are generated at 4.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Study of high performance re-timing using a 40 Gb/s hybrid-integrated Mach-Zehnder all-optical regenerator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We experimentally show that a hybrid-integrated Mach-Zehnder switch with a high performance gate profile allows retiming of optical signals with an accuracy of 500-700 fs even if the input timing jitter is increased to 3 ps.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s WDM-transmission with EDFAs in comparison to Raman amplified transmission with Raman fiber lasers as first-order and second-order pump
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We investigated a 16/spl times/40 Gb/s long-haul transmission to prove whether Raman fiber lasers can replace LDs used for codirectional second-order pumped Raman amplifiers (RA) and compared the RA to counter pumped RA and EDFAs.

articleTitle: Multi-channel residual dispersion compensation in a 40 Gb/s WDM system utilizing a single all-fiber delay line filter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate multi-channel residual dispersion compensation in a 40 Gbit/s optical transmission system with 100 GHz channel spacing using a single adaptive all-fiber delay line filter. The device is based on 3/spl times/3 fiber couplers.

articleTitle: Effects of MPI noise on various modulation formats in distributed Raman amplified system
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We evaluated the effect of MPI noise on various modulation formats in a distributed Raman amplified system. The results show that RZ-DPSK is the most tolerant modulation format to MPI noise.

articleTitle: 4/spl times/4 hard polymer clad fiber (HPCF) splitter for short reach PON system based on HPCF
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report a 4/spl times/4 hard polymer clad fiber splitter using a novel fusion-tapering technique, which showed an insertion loss of 10.50 dB and excess loss of 4.58 dB, with excellent uniformity in power splitting ratio. Eye patterns of throughput for 1.24 and 2.5 Gbps at 820 nm were also measured.

articleTitle: The interaction between fiber PMD and polarization hole burning in long-haul transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show that the effective spectral width of polarization hole-burning is strongly influenced by the transmission fiber's polarization mode dispersion. We give a simplified theory of this effect along with experimental conformation.

articleTitle: Simulation and modeling of the mean time to restore for optical mesh networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We simulate, analyze, and model the mean time to restore failed demands for optical mesh networks survivable under single link failures. The analytic formulation encompasses a variety of network and switch architectures and restoration strategies.

articleTitle: OFK - Resonator and sagnac-based devices
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Rigorous electromagnetic simulations are used to design high-index-contrast microring-resonator filters. The fust fabricated third-order filters compensated for passband distortion due to coupling-induced and fabrication-related fiequency shifts demonstrate a 20nm FSR and the highest reported thru-port extinction (14dB).

articleTitle: Fully-integrated planar-waveguide resonator optics based on holographic Bragg reflectors
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate an integrated concentric Fabry-Perot resonator based on holographic Bragg reflectors. The cavity, fabricated in a low-loss silica-on-silicon slab waveguide using high-fidelity deep ultra violet photolithographic fabrication, exhibits a reflectivity-limited Q-factor of approximately 10/sup 5/.

articleTitle: Vibration tolerant swept wavelength interferometry
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We describe a vibration tolerant coherent interferometer. The spectral phase response of a reference gas cell in the vicinity of an absorption line is measured in the presence of a vibrational disturbance using this method.

articleTitle: Understanding the statistical noise properties of an optical pulse propagating in a nonlinear semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) -experimental and theoretical study
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a theoretical analysis of the statistical properties of the noise accompanying an optical pulse propagating in a saturated SOA. The theoretical predictions show noise redistribution and are confirmed by a series of experiments.

articleTitle: Two-photon absorption induced channel crosstalk in WDM OOK and DPSK
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The effect of two-photon absorption on DPSK and OOK transmission is analyzed by simulation. DPSK is found to have an advantage over OOK in both Q and eye closure penalty for multi-channel WDM transmissions.

articleTitle: Characterization of coherence properties of a free-running sub-kilohertz-linewidth fiber laser by FMCW
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) measurements of Rayleigh backscattering in 85-km fiber derives coherence length of a free-running sub-kilohertz-linewidth fiber laser to be 210 km and the longest distance is measured with FMCW.

articleTitle: Strain-insensitive and high-temperature long-period gratings inscribed in photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate the strain-insensitive and high-temperature long-period gratings in photonic crystal fiber. Thermal dependency of resonance wavelength is 10.9 pm//spl deg/C at range from 24/spl deg/C to 992/spl deg/C, whereas coefficient of strain sensitivity is -0.192 pm//spl mu//spl epsiv/ up to 2.74%/spl epsiv/.

articleTitle: Signal-phase diffusion by fiber-based all-optical 2R regenerators
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Preservation of phase information on the signal by different types of fiber-based all-optical 2R regenerators is numerically studied. A four-wave mixing (FWM)-based regenerator well preserves the phase and is suitable for amplitude regeneration of RZ-DPSK signals.

articleTitle: Novel spectral filters based on holey fiber tapers and fused taper couplers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report novel transmission characteristics of index guiding holey fiber adiabatic tapers and fused taper couplers. Various spectral functionalities of the filters were designed using BPM and spectral responses were experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: PMD properties of spun silica holey fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report the fabrication of a spun holey optical fiber. Measurements of differential group delay (DGD) confirm that significant reductions in polarization mode dispersion (PMD) can be readily achieved using this approach.

articleTitle: Photonics R&D activities in mainland China
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The current status of the main national R&D programs on optical communication systems and network technologies, launched to sustain a rapid growth of telecom networks in mainland China, are reviewed. The research accomplishments of some photonics related R&D projects are presented.

articleTitle: Experiments and modeling of high power Er-Yb doped short fiber lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Generation of 9.3 W cw output from a 7-cm Er-Yb doped phosphate fiber laser was demonstrated experimentally. The performance and intrinsic loss mechanisms of the laser were quantitatively analyzed through modeling.

articleTitle: Polymer fiber Bragg gratings tunable dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a new scheme for tunable dispersion with a large tuning range and a fixed center wavelength using linearly chirped polymer fiber Bragg gratings. Simple tension and uniform heating are employed as the control process.

articleTitle: Novel PDL/PDG compensator for transmission optical devices using Sagnac interferometer
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We describe a novel scheme for complete suppression of polarization-dependent loss/gain (PDL, PDG) for transmission-type optical devices (LPG, SOA) via a /spl lambda//2-shifted all-fiber Sagnac loop interferometer. The results are explained theoretically and demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Recent advances in nanocrystal-Si sensitized, Er-doped silica waveguide amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Recent advances in nanocrystal-Si sensitized, Er-doped silica waveguide amplifiers are introduced. A numerical performance analysis demonstrating its comparative advantages and commercial performance is presented, and ultra-broadband luminescence using a single pump-source and Er-Tm codoping is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Polarization mode coupling along air-silica microstructure fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We use the dramatic change in modal birefringence with wavelength in air-silica microstructure fibers to clarify polarization mode coupling along the fiber. The mode coupling in the fiber is successfully observed using an interferometric method.

articleTitle: Coherent optical frequency domain six-port measurement technique
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A new interferometric approach to measure complex reflection coefficients is presented. It is founded on the successful six-port microwave measurement technique and relies on a six-port planar lightwave circuit (PLC) which has been designed and simulated.

articleTitle: OFB - Fiber structures for advanced amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Characteristics of photonic crystal double clad fibers are introduced. Our research suggests that large numerical aperture in photonic crystal types are effective to reduce harmful non-linear optics in high power amplification.

articleTitle: Gain-flatness improvement over C-band employing silica-based borate/alumina-codoped EDF
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Employing borate/alumina-codoped EDF, the relative gain ripple over the C-band has been reduced to less than 10%, which is to our knowledge the record for the gain flatness of C-band silica-based EDFAs.

articleTitle: Raman gain efficiency measured on 16 Mm of Raman optimized NZDF fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present results for Raman gain efficiency, C/sub R/, of a Raman optimized NZDF, measured on a large-scale production volume of 16000 km. The average value of C/sub R/ is 0.60 (W.km)/sup -1/ with 2.5% standard deviation.

articleTitle: Polarization state control of light by single-walled carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Optical activity was observed in films of vertically aligned single-walled carbon-nanotubes (SWCNTs). We report the control of both the polarization state and transmission of incoming light at 1550 nm by azimuthal and axial tilting of SWNT film about its aligned axis.

articleTitle: Blind-FROG in a quasi-phase-matched LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguide
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate the measurement of short pulses in the 1.55 /spl mu/m telecommunications window by spectrally resolved cross correlation in an integrated LiNbO/sub 3/ device. Extremely high quality pulse retrieval is obtained for pulsewidths down to 4 ps.

articleTitle: Ultra-sensitive dynamic strain detection by phase-sensitive laser frequency locking to a passive Bragg grating resonator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a pico-strain sensing technique by remote interrogation of passive Bragg grating Fabry-Perot resonators, based on the Pound-Drever-Hall technique, used for laser frequency locking and signal extraction. It employs radio-frequency phase modulation to derive error signals.

articleTitle: Forward and backward Brillouin scattering in a holey fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
