abstract: We demonstrate congestion controlled optical burst switching utilizing two-way signaling in field trials. The optical bursts, created in each node with Poisson probability, were routed within 20 ms.

articleTitle: Does optical burst switching have a role in the core network?
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show that optical burst switching (OBS) does not appear to be a viable option for routing in the core network. In order to achieve an acceptably low blocking probability, OBS networks require an uneconomically large increase in network transmission capacity.

articleTitle: Flow control and congestion management for distributed scheduling of burst transmissions in time-domain wavelength interleaved networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The paper presents an algorithm for flow control and congestion management under the time-domain wavelength interleaved optical network architecture (Saniee, I. and Widjaja, I., OFC, 2004). The context of this algorithm is distributed scheduling for servicing asynchronously varying data streams.

articleTitle: ONU authentication technique using loopback modulation within a PON disturbance environment
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An ONU authentication method with extraordinary interference immunity is proposed to specify defective ONU. We successfully demonstrated low-speed data communication for subscriber identification by using ONU loopback on-off-keying modulation and autocorrelation detection within an optically disturbed environment.

articleTitle: Radiation hard optical fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper examines currently existing fibers of nearly all types that show sufficient radiation hardness in lengths necessary for their respective applications. It also considers hydrogen loading or treatment and thermal or photo bleaching which can harden certain fibers or fiber links.

articleTitle: Using optical frequency multiplication to deliver a 17 GHz 64 QAM modulated signal to a simplified radio access unit fed by multimode fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Using optical frequency multiplication, simultaneous 3 GHz to 17 GHz carrier upconversion and 64-QAM modulation with low EVM (4.6 %) is demonstrated. A simplified fiber wireless access unit fed by 4 km multimode fiber is used.

articleTitle: Dynamics of fiber fuse propagation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The dynamics of the fiber fuse effect, including the process of bubble formation in the fiber core, was investigated for the first time. Bubbles in the core were observed not later than 20-70 /spl mu/s after the passing of the plasma leading edge.

articleTitle: 40-Gbps waveguide avalanche photodiodes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Thin multiplication waveguide avalanche photodiodes have been developed for use in 40-Gbit/s receivers. High responsivity of 0.73-0.88 A/W, wide bandwidth of 30-35 GHz, and gain-bandwidth product of 140-180 GHz have realized the receiver sensitivity of -19 dBm at 40 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: All-optical analog-to-digital conversion by slicing supercontinuum spectrum and switching with nonlinear optical loop mirror
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a novel all-optical analog-to-digital conversion scheme consisting of quantization by slicing supercontinuum spectrum and coding by switching pulses with a nonlinear optical loop mirror. The proposed scheme is experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: A novel star-ring protection architecture scheme for WDM passive optical access networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a star-ring network architecture and wavelength assignment scheme for multi-wavelength passive optical networks with full path protection capability. Bi-directional traffic can be restored promptly for single/multiple link failure scenarios.

articleTitle: Efficient dynamic bandwidth allocation based on upstream broadcast in Ethernet passive optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a novel dynamic bandwidth allocation scheme that exploits a physical layer architecture to facilitate upstream broadcast in an EPON. The network meets stringent QoS requirements, achieves high channel utilization and optimizes downstream capacity.

articleTitle: Bidirectional wavelength-division-multiplexing self-healing passive optical network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a bidirectional wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) self-healing passive optical network (PON), which can provide 1+1 protection capability. In this network, self-healing can be achieved within 8 ms against any fiber cut of the feeder fiber and the distribution fiber.

articleTitle: High-speed QKD system synchronized by automatic phase-alignment mechanism
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A high-speed QKD system, which has an automatic modulation-phase-alignment mechanism for compensating for GVD, was developed. Using this system, we confirmed high-speed and stable quantum key distribution with transmission over 40 km was possible.

articleTitle: High power fiber lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Over 1 kW of output power has now been reached with nearly diffraction-limited ytterbium-doped fiber lasers. Amplifiers can reach comparable powers, even with single-frequency beams. We review these and other recent results and discuss the possibilities for further progress.

articleTitle: Apodization of a multichannel dispersion compensator by phase modulation coding of a phase mask
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A very simple fabrication process for multichannel fiber Bragg grating (FBG) dispersion compensators is demonstrated by phase modulation coding of both the apodization profile and the phase sampling in a phase mask.

articleTitle: Cladding-pumped Raman fiber amplifier for high-gain, high-energy single-stage amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A cladding-pumped Raman-fiber amplifier for single-mode pulses is demonstrated. A small-signal gain of nearly 50 dB is reached at 1663 nm. The use of multimode pump pulses opens up for high-energy pulse amplification. We obtain a power-conversion-efficiency of 36%.

articleTitle: Demonstration of user-controlled network interface for subwavelength bandwidth-on-demand services
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents the hardware architecture for a user-controlled network interface supporting sub-wavelength bandwidth-on-demand services. Results show the architecture is well suited for mapping user traffic into optical packets or bursts directly controlled by the user.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of optical CDMA networks with random media access schemes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis approach for OCDMA networks, which takes into account both the physical layer characteristics and random media access schemes. Analysis results demonstrate its effectiveness in characterizing the OCDMA network dynamics.

articleTitle: A lead silicate holey fiber with /spl gamma/=1860 W/sup -1/km/sup -1/ at 1550 nm
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report the fabrication of lead silicate holey fibers with record nonlinearities of up to 1860 W/sup -1/m/sup -1/ at 1.55 /spl mu/m. Broadband supercontinuum generation is obtained in a dispersion optimized fiber variant at /spl sim/100 pJ pulse energies for 1.06 /spl mu/m pumping.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated diplexer chip for PON applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A novel, compact diplexer chip for PON applications has been demonstrated by monolithic integration of an etched facet 1310 nm horizontal cavity surface-emitting laser with a 1490 nm PIN detector. Optical characteristics, sensitivity, and isolation are reported.

articleTitle: Long term PMD characterization of installed G.652 fibers in a metropolitan network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We investigated the long-term PMD (polarization mode dispersion) behavior of a metropolitan G.652 fiber plant of a major Italian telecom operator, installed in Turin, Italy. We found that the expected Maxwellian distribution is not always achieved, as well as other statistical anomalies.

articleTitle: Influence of polarization scattering on polarization-assisted OSNR monitoring in dense WDM systems with NZ-DSF and Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show experimentally that the inter-channel XPM induced polarization scattering can cause large errors for polarization-assisted OSNR monitoring techniques in a dense WDM system with NZ-DSF, Raman amplification and RZ modulation signals.

articleTitle: Impairments of bit-to-bit alternate-polarization on non-linear threshold, CD and DGD tolerance of 43 Gb/s ASK and DPSK formats [fibre optic communication]
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Applying bit-to-bit alternate-polarization modulation at 43 Gb/s in ASK/DPSK formats, we found experimentally non-linear threshold benefits up to 4 dB with RZ and 2 dB with NRZ, reduction of DGD tolerance up to 3 ps with RZ formats and a dispersion-tolerance of 20% with DPSK-NRZ.

articleTitle: Tunable MEMS devices for reconfigurable optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Transmitters and receivers based on MEMS-tuned external cavity diode lasers and diffraction grating filters deployed in reconfigurable optical networks provide up to 6.4 THz tuning in 15 ms with /spl plusmn/1.25 GHz frequency accuracy and superior optical performance in compact packages.

articleTitle: Advances in planar lightwave circuits
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Advances in silica-on-silicon planar lightwave circuit (PLC) technology are enabling a higher level of integration for reconfigurable add/drop multiplexers. Newer integrated optics materials systems offer important advantages in cost and performance.

articleTitle: Experimental GMPLS fault management for OULSR transport networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a novel GMPLS-based fault management architecture for OULSR rings tested in the ADRENALINE testbed. Experimental results show an optical protection delay of 45 ms using SNMP-based monitoring and IP/control restoration delays around 2100 ms.

articleTitle: Development of MEMS-based optical surge suppressor
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A MEMS-based optical surge suppressor is proposed. The device consists of MEMS-shutter and photovoltaic detector that triggers the shutter through in-line monitoring of surge light around power level of 10dBm with insertion loss of 1.5dB.

articleTitle: Homodyne phase-shift-keying systems: past challenges and future opportunities
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Homodyne phase-shift-keying systems can achieve the best sensitivity and the longest transmission distance. This paper reviews past research efforts and examines future possibilities in this field.

articleTitle: Noise induced by distributed Raman amplification in a forward-pumping scheme using FBG-stabilized diodes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Forward Raman amplification using FBG-stabilized diodes yields higher signal RIN than expected from the Raman-gain-mediated transfer function. We demonstrate that this extra noise originates from pump-signal nonlinear parametric interactions, even far from the phase-matching condition.

articleTitle: Sixth-order cascaded Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Sixth-order Raman amplification is demonstrated for the first time and shown to provide >10 dB budget improvement. Raman amplifiers of differing orders are compared in several commercial fibers and optimal Raman gains are presented.

articleTitle: Simplified optical coupling and alignment scheme for cost effective 10 Gbit/s TOSA modules based on edge emitters hermetically packaged in micro-machined silicon structures
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Packaging of opto-electronic components - as opposed to semiconductor or electronics ICs - requires not only hermeticity but also proper alignment of optical elements. Due to tolerances in the range of a few microns at best, conventional technology usually requires laborious active alignment steps to couple light efficiently into the fiber. A simple optical coupling and alignment scheme is presented which enables the fabrication of cost effective 10 Gbit/s TOSA (transmitter optical sub-assembly) modules which are based on edge-emitting laser diodes packaged hermetically in micro-machined silicon structures.

articleTitle: Fabrication of wavelength splitter designed by wavefront matching method
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report the first fabrication of a waveguide device designed using our recently proposed wavefront matching method. We fabricated a very compact wavelength splitter having mosaic-like patterns, and confirmed its operation in experiments.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of connection setup in GMPLS IP optical network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper investigates the efficiency of deploying RSVP-TE for connection setup in GMPLS IP optical networks. The call blocking probability will be dramatically increased if the network-wide call inter-arrival time is within the concretion setup delay.

articleTitle: Improving bending losses in holey fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Preliminary work has shown that the bending losses of large-mode-area holey fibers can be improved by modifying the hole configuration (Mortensen et al. (2003)). For the first time, we accurately quantify the advantages of this technique.

articleTitle: New dispersion decreasing fiber with high SBS threshold for nonlinear signal processing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A new dispersion decreasing fiber with reduced stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) by changing the core refractive index was designed and fabricated. SBS threshold improvement of 7 dB over the conventional nonlinear fiber was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Polarization interleaving to reduce inter-channel nonlinear penalties in polarization multiplexed transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We investigate through simulations and experiments inter-channel nonlinear penalties in 2/spl times/10 Gbit/s NRZ polarization-multiplexed transmission. We show that the inter-channel nonlinear penalties can be partially mitigated by polarization interleaved transmission of the polarization-multiplexed channels.

articleTitle: Upstream experiments on the gigabit PON physical medium layer
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We give a first time demonstration of a high performance 1.25 Gbit/s GPON burst-mode uplink exceeding the ITU-T G.984 recommendation and supporting power leveling mechanism (PLM). A burst-mode receiver sensitivity of -31.6 dBm was achieved with a dynamic range of 21.9 dB.

articleTitle: Polysiloxane based optical waveguide equipped with fiber guides by using direct photolithography technique
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Fabrication of polysiloxane based optical waveguide with fiber guides by using a direct photolithography technique was developed. The precise patterned fiber guides allowed performing a simple and cost saving alignment without use of fiber arrays.

articleTitle: Low loss (/spl sim/1.4 dB) 200 GHz-16ch athermal AWG compact module for metro/access network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have developed a low loss (/spl sim/1.4dB) 200 GHz-16ch athermal AWG compact module for a metro/access network. A size of the module was achieved a reduction of about 35% in comparison with the conventional module.

articleTitle: Micro-machined XY stage for fiber optics module alignment
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A novel silicon micro-machined XY stage with a hybrid micro-lens for fiber optics module alignment is presented. A MEMS micro-alignment method and silicon chip design are described. Finally the micro-fabricated device performance is discussed.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s fast-locking all-optical packet clock recovery
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate instantaneous 40 Gbit/s clock extraction from 1 ns long data packets separated by 750 ps. The circuit comprises a Fabry-Perot filter and an all-optical power limiting gate and requires very short inter-packet guardbands.

articleTitle: SBS threshold of segmented fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a rigorous analysis of stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in nonuniform fibers consisting of segments with non-overlapping Brillouin gain spectra (BGS). For a span of two segments we predict the optimum configuration with maximum SBS threshold. Theoretical results agree well with measured values.

articleTitle: Dense WDM-PON based on wavelength locked Fabry-Perot lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate 12-channel WDM-PON with 50 GHz channel spacing based on low cost wavelength locked Fabry-Perot laser diodes. The proposed WDM-PON can accommodate 80 channels with an EDFA based broadband light source.

articleTitle: Waveguide design of InGaAs/AlAs/AlAsSb inter-subband transition optical switch
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: An InGaAs/AlAs/AlAsSb inter-subband transition optical switch waveguide is designed for low driving energy. By applying a narrow high-mesa waveguide and thin barriers, the driving energy decreases significantly compared to the conventional ridge structure.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of electrical equalization of differential mode delay in MMF links for 10-Gigabit Ethernet
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Through statistical analysis of a large number of worst-case multimode fiber channels, we demonstrate that using electrical equalization, the 300 m-transmission reach at 10 Gb/s can be guaranteed for installed multimode fiber under any launch condition.

articleTitle: Optimal WDM layer partitioning and transmission reach in optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We investigate WDM layer network cost in typical North American networks and show that optical transparency at degree 2 and system reach between 1000-2000 km is sufficient for traffic loads between 1 -13 Tb/s.

articleTitle: Timing-jitter in high bit-rate WDM communication systems due to PMD-nonlinearity interaction
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We show that the interaction of polarization-mode-dispersion and cross-phase-modulation in 10 and 40 Gbit/s WDM systems results in a significant timing-jitter, even in the absence of a PMD compensator. An acceptable PMD level can generate unacceptable jitter in WDM systems.

articleTitle: Wide temperature range (0 to 85/spl deg/C), 40-km SMF transmission of a 1.55 /spl mu/m, 10-Gbit/s InGaAlAs electroabsorption modulator integrated DFB laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A new uncooled 1.55 /spl mu/m InGaAlAs electroabsorption-modulator integrated DFB-laser suitable for low-power-consumption 10-Gbit/s small-form-factor modules is demonstrated. For the first time, 10-Gbit/s 40-km normal SMF transmission with 1-dB power penalty is achieved from 0 to 85/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Optimal receiver bandwidths, bit error probabilities and chromatic dispersion tolerance of 40Gbit/s optical 8-DPSK with NRZ and RZ impulse shaping
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: For the first time, optimal optical and electrical receiver bandwidths, bit error probabilities and chromatic dispersion tolerance of optical differential 8-level phase-shift keying are studied using a Karhunen-Loeve based semi-analytical method.

articleTitle: Verizon's fiber to the premises: lessons learned
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: To make FTTP a reality, various architectural choices have to be made to make the technology, its adoption by the customer and its deployment cost effective. The paper reviews such decisions and outlines some of the lessons learned in the last six months that Verizon has deployed FTTP.

articleTitle: High-responsivity high-speed and high-power partially depleted absorber waveguide photodiodes with relaxed coupling tolerances
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We reported a partially depleted absorber evanescently coupled waveguide photodiode that achieves 17 mA saturation current, 0.81 A/W responsivity, >50 GHz bandwidth and /spl plusmn/2.0 /spl mu/m (/spl plusmn/1.3 /spl mu/m) horizontal (vertical) -1 dB coupling tolerances.

articleTitle: Adaptive PMD compensation for 170 Gbit/s RZ transmission systems with alternating polarisation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report on adaptive PMD (polarisation mode dispersion) compensation in a 170 Gbit/s RZ transmission system with alternating polarisation. The PMD tolerance is significantly improved using an asymmetric rather than symmetric setup of the two-stage PMD compensator.

articleTitle: Modeling the non-linear index of optical fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and validate experimentally a simple model that allows us to calculate the nonlinear index, n/sub 2/, of any fiber type. Single-mode and higher-order-mode dispersion-compensating fibers (DCF) are investigated and n/sub 2/ dependence on chromatic dispersion is analyzed.

articleTitle: Transmission of 40 Gb/s WDM signals over 6,250 km of conventional NZ-DSF with >4 dB FEC margin
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We successfully transmitted 18/spl times/40 Gb/s RZ-DPSK channels over 6,250 km of non-slope-matched-fibers with >4 dB FEC margin using dispersion-slope compensators at the receiver. We demonstrated that 40 Gb/s DPSK worked as well as 10 Gb/s RZ-OOK for the same spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Variation of PMD-induced outage rates and durations with link length on buried standard single-mode fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: From first-order polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) outage analysis using measured differential group delay (DGD) data on buried standard single-mode fibers, we observed that the outage rates increase monotonically with link length, although not linearly.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a multicast-capable optical-label switching router
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper proposes and demonstrates an optical-label switching router with limited multicast capability. A multi-wavelength converter is the key sub-system enabling packet replication. The experimental demonstration shows correct packet multicast forwarding.

articleTitle: Dual-wavelength pumped TDFAs for S-band optical telecommunication - an evaluation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Different dual-wavelength pumping schemes for thulium-doped fiber amplifiers (TDFA) are characterized and evaluated for their feasibility in S-band optical telecommunication networks. The main focus is on system impairments due to transient effects, gain cross-saturation, and bit error rate.

articleTitle: System outage probability due to dispersion variation caused by seasonal and regional temperature variations
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We evaluated the system outage probability of high-speed optical network caused by the variation of chromatic dispersion arising from the seasonal and regional temperature variations.

articleTitle: Using divisible load theory to dimension optical transport networks for computational grids
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Using the notion of divisible load, this paper attempts to shed light on the operational cost of an optical transport network when used to connect different sites of a computational grid.

articleTitle: Effects of DGE channel bandwidth on nonlinear ULH systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Experiments and simulations show that the channel bandwidth of a dynamic gain-equalizer (DGE) exerts strong influence on the performance of a nonlinear ULH (ultra-long haul) system. For a 40-channel, 6000-km, 100 GHz-spaced DWDM system with 12.5 Gb/s data rate, the optimal bandwidth is near 50 GHz.

articleTitle: Minimum-cost topology adaptation for an ISP's mesh network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a topology adaptation model for Internet service providers for minimizing their total dollar-cost for network operations. We observe significant cost-savings of 21% on a nationwide network employing realistic traffic models and bandwidth cost.

articleTitle: Heavy metal oxide glass holey fibers with high nonlinearity
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report on the development of small-core high-NA lead silicate and bismuth glass holey fibers. We measured high nonlinearity (1100 W/sup -1/ km/sup -1/ in bismuth holey fiber) and predicted near-zero or anomalous dispersion at 1550 nm.

articleTitle: Compact and low power consumption 16 /spl times/ 16 optical matrix switch with silica-based PLC technology
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We successfully reduced the chip size of a 16/spl times/16 optical matrix switch with silica-based planar lightwave circuit technology to 36 %, and the power consumption to 37 % by employing 1.5 % /spl Delta/ waveguides, heat insulating grooves, and a new circuit layout.

articleTitle: Optical pulse generator using phase modulator and chirped fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate an optical pulse generator, in which CW light is modulated by a phase modulator and compressed into pulses by linearly chirped fiber Bragg gratings. Two types of pulse are generated by changing the conditions.

articleTitle: Microwave signal transmission over a directly-modulated radio-over-fiber link using cascaded semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a record 150 km transmission of microwave signals by a directly-modulated radio-over-fiber link with a bit-error-rate of less than 10/sup -12/. Cascaded semiconductor optical amplifiers are employed to extend the length of the transmission link.

articleTitle: Single-mode performance in multimode fibre devices
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a waveguide transition between a multimode fibre and several single-mode fibres. Splicing identical Bragg gratings between two such transitions yields a multimode fibre filter with the transmission spectrum of a single-mode fibre grating.

articleTitle: 50 GHz directly-modulated injection-locked 1.55 /spl mu/m VCSELs
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The resonance frequency of several 1.55 /spl mu/m VCSELs is enhanced from 7 GHz up to /spl sim/50 GHz with the optical injection locking technique. This is the highest value reported for directly modulated lasers.

articleTitle: High resolution and high speed wavelength-parallel polarization sensor for dense WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report on a wavelength-parallel polarization sensor with potential to perform /spl les/ 4 GHz-spaced sub-channel polarization measurement for multiple dense WDM channels in parallel, with measurement time of less than 5 ms.

articleTitle: Architectures and performance of fiber delay line buffers in packet-based multifiber optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we study the architectures and performance of fiber delay line (FDL) buffers in packet-based multifiber optical networks. Three buffering architectures are considered and their performance are evaluated and compared through extensive simulation.

articleTitle: Multiple wavelength conversion with gain by high repetition-rate pulsed-pump fiber OPA
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel multiple wavelength converter with gain based on a pulsed-pump fiber optical parametric device. Penalties ranging from 0.26 to 1.24 dB for /spl plusmn/k /spl times/100 GHz (k= 1,2,3,4) wavelength conversion were measured.

articleTitle: Mode-locked fiber lasers using vertically aligned carbon nanotubes directly synthesized onto substrates
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate novel passively mode-locked fiber lasers using vertically aligned carbon nanotubes synthesized using the low-temperature alcohol catalytic CVD method. We found that the laser can be mode locked at wide range of slant angles.

articleTitle: Ad-fiber widely tunable raman laser in a combined linear and sagnac-loop configuration
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a widely tunable cascaded all-fiber Raman laser in a combined linear and Sagnac-loop configuration which provides an output power of several hundred milliwatts and a tuning range of 120 nm without employing any bulk-optical devices

articleTitle: 320 Gb/s single-polarization OTDM transmission over 80 km standard transmission fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Optical time-division multiplexing (OTDM) is an attractive technique for increasing the capacity of optical transmission systems. 320 Gbit/s single-channel and single-polarization error-free transmission over continuous spans of either 80 km SMF or 77 km NZDSF are realized.

articleTitle: Two-photon absorption in semiconductor optical amplifiers: a non-adiabatic theoretical approach
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: A non-adiabatic theoretical model including all fast gain dynamics in SOAs is presented. It emerges that an adiabatic theory cannot properly describe the impact of the TPA on high-energy ultrafast pulses propagating in SOAs.

articleTitle: Performance of IP over optical networks with dynamic bandwidth allocation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: IP over optical network performance can be improved with dynamic bandwidth allocation, depending on the reallocation paradigm and the network topology. Under high connectivity, dynamic bandwidth allocation provides a notable boost to the network's traffic-carrying capacity.

articleTitle: Optical wireless networks: transceiver distribution provisioning
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a transceiver-distribution provisioning heuristic for optimized optical wireless networks. Simulation results show that networks adopting the proposed heuristic outperform on load balance, link usage, and average packet delay by 37%, 29%, and 17%, respectively, compared to unplanned transceiver distribution.

articleTitle: Thulium doped fiber amplifier for the first window from 790 nm to 850 nm with 690 nm/1400 nm dual pumping
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate an optical amplifier with 30 dB gain for the 850 nm window using specialized fiber and practical pumping wavelengths of 690 nm and 1400 nm. The experimental results were achieved after thorough calculations, made by molecular dynamics simulation, provided guidance on physical parameters.

articleTitle: Exploiting connection-holding time to improve resource efficiency for dynamic provisioning in shared-path protection
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: For dynamic provisioning of shared-path-protected connections in an optical mesh network, we investigate a new algorithm which exploits the holding time of connections to achieve significant reduction in resource overbuild.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a microfiber loop optical resonator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a microfiber loop optical resonator. At telecommunication wavelengths, it achieves loaded and intrinsic Q-factors of 95000 and 630000, respectively. As an example, the resonator performs as an ultrafast gas contact temperature sensor.

articleTitle: A single-mode Tm-doped double-clad optical fiber amplifier operating at 843 nm wavelength
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report a novel single-mode Tm-doped amplifier optimized for the first-window optical communication wavelength band. A peak gain of about 22.5 dB at 843 nm and a full-width-half-maximum wavelength band of about 20 nm have been obtained.

articleTitle: 100 mW phase-shifted 1550 nm BH DFB arrays with a 10-micron pitch
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Very high yield arrays with excellent linewidth, RIN, and SMSR are demonstrated. In a tunable laser application, we obtained 50 mW fiber coupled power over a 39 nm continuous range by temperature tuning from 15 C to 45 C.

articleTitle: Photonic integration on InP for telecom and datacom applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The current and future role of photonic InP integration in order to provide suitable single chip components for telecom and datacom markets is emphasized under the requirement of existing alternative and complementary technologies.

articleTitle: Next generation high-speed multimode fiber links and their specifications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.

articleTitle: Design of waveguide grating routers for simultaneous multiple optical code generation in photonic MPLS networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We review novel methods to generate optical codes for use in MPLS or CDM transmission. A standard WGR can be designed to generate simultaneously a large number of highly orthogonal codes as a result of a single input pulse.

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion of thin film filters
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper discusses the chromatic dispersion effects of thin film filters used in telecommunications systems. ITU channel, banded architecture, and low dispersion filter results are presented. Design techniques to improve and manage chromatic dispersion in practical network implementations are discussed.

articleTitle: Instantaneous clock recovery for burst-mode optical label and payload by using a conventional data receiver
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have demonstrated a novel method using a conventional receiver to detect preamble free label and payload in burst-mode transmission in an optical label switched network. The extracted clock exhibits shows small jitter, which can be used for clock recovery and data regeneration.

articleTitle: Forward error control in passive optical network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: BCH codes are proposed for use in PON systems to mitigate the effect of MPN and relax the requirements on laser sources. Different BCH codes are examined and their performances are discussed.

articleTitle: Advances in optical access networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The EPON (Ethernet passive optical network) standard (IEEE 802.3ah) only covers physical and data link layers; the rest is considered out-of-scope. This article explores several interesting research problems brought forward by the EPON architecture, but left out by the standard.

articleTitle: ROADM enabled optimization in WDM rings
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Deployment of reconfigurable OADMs in WDM rings is expected to bring large operational savings. Such nodes also enable online network optimization; we quantify the potential savings as a function of element functionality and traffic churn.

articleTitle: Photodetector linearization using adaptive electronic post-distortion
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: Photodetector linearization using a monolithic CMOS polynomial generator is demonstrated. Improvements of 32.5 dB and 7.2 dB are demonstrated for the 2/sup nd/ order and 3/sup rd/ order input intercept point, respectively.

articleTitle: Performance of a label erase and wavelength switching sub-system for layer-3 all-optical label switching using a two stage InP wavelength converter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We experimentally assess the performance of a two-stage wavelength conversion label swapping sub-system operating at OC-48 line-rates and variable length packets with layer-3 traffic control. Wavelength switching times < 6 ns are observed giving insignificant throughput penalties for dynamic wavelength switching.

articleTitle: A monolithic ultra-compact InP O-CDMA encoder with planarization by HVPE regrowth
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report a monolithic, ultra-compact optical-CDMA encoder/decoder photonic chip in InP with surface planarization by low-pressure hydride-vapor-phase-epitaxy regrowth. The chip consists of an AWG pair and eight electro-optic phase shifters and demonstrated excellent encoding operation.

articleTitle: 40-Gb/s S-band WDM transmission over installed fiber links using erbium-based fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate 8/spl times/40-Gb/s WDM transmission in the S-band using only erbium-based amplifier technology. It is shown that these amplifiers enable transmission over multiple non-optimized spans of installed SSMF in the Deutsche Telekom network of Berlin.

articleTitle: A semiconductor tunable laser using a wavelength selective reflector based on ring resonators
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a tunable laser incorporating a cleavage-free wavelength selective reflector (WSR) formed by buried heterostructure (BH) microring resonators. Utilizing the proposed tunable reflector, a compact, 100-GHz-channel-spaced tunable laser is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Fabrication of dispersion controlled and polarization maintaining photonic crystal fiber for high performance systems and devices
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper reports on the characteristics of the polarization maintaining photonic crystal fiber and shows that it is at a level of practical use. We also discuss the dispersion-flattened photonic crystal fiber designed for nonlinear optics application.

articleTitle: Cancellation of intensity noise caused by stimulated Brillouin scattering in an optical fiber transmission system
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 2005.
abstract: The primary source of broadband intensity noise on an SBS-degraded optical signal is found to be deterministic and depend on the imaginary part of the Brillouin loss spectrum. The noise is reduced by subsequent transmission through a Brillouin amplifier.
